findings.reason: The protected query correctly evaluates every expression but sorts the complete E-row result even though the source explicitly permits any order. That presentation-only ORDER BY can add O(E log E) worst-case work to a branch requiring O(V+E). The inert candidate removes only this sort, preserves the relational result exactly, and meets the stated linear logical bound.

The two role-specific joins resolve exactly the stored values named by each expression: Variables.name is unique and both operand references are guaranteed to exist, so neither join drops or multiplies a row. The legal operator selects the corresponding integer relation, explicit string literals encode its truth value, and every output row retains the originating expression fields.

An independent Python oracle built a name-to-integer mapping and dispatched comparisons without SQL. It, the candidate, protected app query, exact immutable native query, a separately structured resolved-values SQL control, and a correct slower correlated-lookup control agreed on all nine visible cases and all three existing benchmark tiers.

Seed 1440 generated 5,000 schema-valid databases containing 341,934 unique expression triples. Coverage included 151 empty expression sets, 4,110 databases with same-variable operands, 972 forced equal-value pairs under different names, 1,762 databases with unreferenced variables, all three operators, shuffled rows, zero, signed values, and integer endpoints. The candidate, protected query, and independent join control matched the direct Python oracle throughout; the correlated control also matched on 300 additional randomized databases.

Visible trials cover a one-variable one-expression minimum, an empty Expressions table, the signed 32-bit endpoints, same-name comparisons, equal values under different names, values whose ordering contradicts their names, and Variables rows that must not create output. All results use unordered-table validation as required by the source.

Across three real-test repetitions, the candidate passed all nine ordinary outputs and all three benchmark outputs with extra growth exponent approximately 0.00 and largest runtime ratio 0.94x through 0.96x. The independently correct O(VE) correlated control passed every output but failed only scaling each time, with relative growth exponent +0.77 through +0.78 and largest ratio 10.81x through 10.86x.

The three existing benchmark tiers remain hidden and performance-only. Their positive unique sizes S=128, 512, and 2,048 span 16x, contain equal numbers of variables and expressions, and exercise two operand lookups plus every comparison path. The slower correlated query completes normally and fails only scaling, so benchmark.json was not edited.

The complete Approach explicitly targets candidate.sql and derives its two role-specific joins, operator dispatch, one-row-per-expression argument, and omission of any presentation sort. It proves O(V+E) logical time and space and covers correlated lookups, a single-alias failure, the protected sort, name-versus-value semantics, same operands, equal values, signed extremes, unreferenced variables, empty expressions, exact output spelling, and unrestricted order.

All nine ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials. The one authenticated source example now appears exactly with all six expressions and outputs; the two invented legacy samples were reclassified as trials, the hidden real case was replaced visibly, and every expected table is explicitly order-insensitive.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode database problem 1440 and SQL as the active language. The reviewed artifacts preserve both table schemas, primary keys, the three-value operator enum, guaranteed operand references, textual true/false output, and unrestricted row order. The authenticated source contains no separate constraints, hints, notes, images, diagrams, or follow-up.

The protected app and immutable native SQL sources bound to verified submission 2069099669 remain byte-identical and unchanged, as does submission.json. The no-sort replacement exists only as candidate.sql; it has not been submitted, promoted, or represented as remotely Accepted.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed both schemas and key facts, the operator enum and operand guarantee, any-order result contract, one exact six-expression example with explanation, five logical source tables, and no ancillary sections or visuals. source_fidelity.json binds five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 7ff1ac240ca6d72d5755fd2ffb8a2527c75dfd2ec8c9a0867d4078238bf66df3 and validates without errors.
